candidates.worst_problem: The party at centre-left is packed into one tight line. At 1600x900 and 1280x800 the Kids' bodies merge, and Bones, Wisp and Count Crumbula pile at their feet, with the chinchilla half hidden behind Wisp, so the group reads as a queue rather than four distinct pairs. The upper-left plates are the brightest and most sample-like of the set.

The two-rank staging has real depth and all four Kids read, but Bones is half tucked behind Mateo's shins and Wisp is small and pushed to the rear at both sizes. The upper-left plates also lose the samples' closed frame: the left side stays open, the ground is murky maroon, and the Weak 2 tag hangs off the edge.

Two Kids are almost lost: Amina is reduced to a tuft of hair and Mateo to a sliver behind Eli, while Wisp hides behind Maya and Bones behind legs. Eli also covers the HOUSE RULE sign at 1280x800 (it reads USE RULE). The upper-left plates are thin dark web rectangles with no cartouche presence.

This is the clearest party of the four: large Kids and all four Companions spread in a front rank. Even so, Amina is still half masked behind Maya and Eli, and at 1280x800 Eli's hand and lens press against the door enemy, so the front edge of the group needs air. The plates are well framed but remain plain purple bars, not painted cartouches.

All 14 controls are present, and the portrait pins plus the four-medallion vote strip answer who chose which door instantly at both sizes. However, the bottom toolbar's flat tan tiles, flat pink Eraser and ghosted grey Undo and Clear read as a skinned button row on a ruler more than as drawn tools. The tan Discoveries and How to play tiles have the same flatness.

The ruler, brass rail, pencils and pinned paper letter tags are properly objects on a table, and all 14 controls are present. But friends are reduced to single letters on the map, and the vote strip drops its portraits for a parchment scrap, so the door read is slower. The dark zoom buttons at the right of the rail are faint, and tile labels get tight at 1280x800.

The notes toolbar is a flat dark web panel of thin-outlined rectangular buttons covering the bottom of the map at both sizes, and Undo and Clear are faint. The friends' door tags are tiny low-contrast brown strips, and the Discoveries and How to play buttons are plain rounded web buttons.

The mahogany tray with big pencils and a ruler section is the most convincing single object, and all 14 controls are legible. But it rides high over the map: at 1280x800 it half covers the lower door and leaves NOT a coat rack peeking out beneath it. The door tags are letter-only plaques, slower to read than faces.

The plate hangs on chains from the top bar with a candle medallion and clears every enemy sign at both sizes, so it looks deliberate. Its message still wraps to leave a short widow, back in., and the crowded party beneath it is the screen's weakest part.

The hung plate clears all enemy signs at both sizes, and its one-line message is the cleanest read. However, the broken-link glyph in the left medallion reads as a UI icon rather than an object from the house, and the hanging rods are so thin the plate nearly floats.

The plain rounded rectangle at top centre covers the HOUSE RULE medallion and clips its sign at both sizes, and at 1280x800 it also cuts off Kids' heads, so it fails the visibility test and looks like a web toast.

The right-wall plate clears all enemy signs and has a good crown medallion, but it is tall and stacked. It blots out the candle sconce, sits within a few pixels of the BUFF sign at 1280x800, and reads more like a side popover than something hung in the room.

Nothing collides at either size, but the wall below the seats is thin, with one tiny window oddly low and a lone rope. The seed sits in a bright gold pill between the footer buttons that looks like a web chip, and GO IN TOGETHER at lower right is very faint.

The pinned blueprint, red pencil, T-square and rope make the wall below the seats a real treehouse and collide with nothing at either size, and the seed stamped on the parchment is the best idea on the board. That stamp is thin red on tan and hard to read, and the footer stays comparatively bare.

At 1600x900 the window and rope peer out cut off from behind seats 1 and 4, while at 1280x800 the wall is emptied entirely. The bare italic line under the banner runs across the stars and window edge without a surface behind it, and at 1600x900 it collides with a star at its end.

The pinned parchment, string-tied number tag and gold-ruled nameplates are strong and collide with nothing, but the wall below the seats stays sparse with only a tiny window and small rope. The squared plates are less like the samples' notched cartouches, and GO IN TOGETHER at lower right is faint.

The rules panels have a mottled painted surface with worn corners that blends fairly well, but the rules text in the middle of each panel stays small with large dead space around it at both sizes, and the saturated teal and red fields look slightly airbrushed.

The embossed damask gives the rules panels the richest surface, and the large text fills them and reads best at both sizes. But the cloth is bright and busy and stops at a hard edge under the frame, so it edges toward a pasted swatch, especially the blue fields.

The rules panels are nearly black with a damask and shield watermark so faint that at both sizes they read as an empty dark box with small text floating in it, which is calm through absence rather than a surface.

The tooled-leather rules panels have a real grain and inner rule, but the washed grey-blue and dusty brown look lifted from another palette and sit like pasted swatches beneath the card art. The rules text also stays small inside them at both sizes.

winner_fixes: map-vote, door tags on the map: the pinned paper letters identify friends slowly. Keep the pinned paper but add each friend's painted Kid portrait beside the letter, so the chosen door reads at a glance at 1600x900 and 1280x800.
map-vote, bottom-centre vote strip: the parchment scrap has no portraits. Set the four Kid medallions into the parchment beside 3 of 4 have chosen, with the undecided friend's medallion dimmed.

combat-party, Companions at the party's feet: Bones is half behind Mateo's shins and Wisp is small and at the rear. Bring all four Companions into a clear front rank at their full scale, keeping the two-rank depth of the Kids.

combat-party, the three upper-left plates: the open left side and murky maroon ground drift from the samples. Close them with a full gold double rule and notched corners on an aubergine ground, and seat the Weak 2 tag inside the plate instead of hanging off its edge.

map-vote, right end of the brass rail: the minus and plus zoom buttons are dark and faint. Paint them as round purple enamel buttons with bright gold rims, like the samples' round buttons, at their present size or larger.

map-vote, wooden tile labels at 1280x800: Undo, Clear, X room and You are here sit tight in their tiles with dark type on mid tan. Lighten the tile faces and give the words more room in the tiles, without reducing type size or dropping any control.

shop, the blue and red rules panels: the damask ends at a hard edge under the frame and verges on a pasted swatch. Add candle-side falloff, darkened and worn edges and a soft inner shadow from the gold rule, keeping the large text exactly as large.

net-plate, the plate at upper right: the broken-link glyph reads as a UI icon and the hanging rods are hair thin. Replace the glyph with a painted guttering candle or frayed rope and draw real chains from the top bar.
lobby-party, the parchment stamp HOUSE NO. 609573837: thin red on tan is hard to read at both sizes. Make it a heavier, darker ink stamp with more room on the parchment, enlarging it if needed.
lobby-party, the blueprint at lower left: it is the flattest of the wall objects. Give it curled corners, a cast shadow and warmer candle light so it sits with the pencil and T-square.

grafts.idea: Map door pins that carry the friend's painted Kid portrait with a letter tag on a stem, which makes each friend's door choice instant.
The vote strip's row of four Kid medallions, with the undecided friend's medallion dimmed.
The candle medallion on the lost-connection plate, an in-world object in place of a link icon, with chains heavy enough to see.
The combat staging of larger Kids with every Companion clear in a front rank, which is the most recognisable party of the four.
The mahogany tray under the pencils and the active Hand block's lit highlight, which give the notes toolbar more weight and a clear current-tool state.
The fuller purple-ground plates with closed gold frames in combat's upper left.

verdicts.verdict: No candidate reaches reference fit: coherence stays below 9 on every screen, and none could pass as painted by the samples' hand. LARIMAR is the clear loser. It has flat web panels on the map and net plate, hides two Kids, covers the HOUSE RULE sign, and at 1600x900 leaves a window and rope cut off behind the seats while emptying that wall at 1280x800. VARISCITE is the best system, narrowly. Its drawn draughtsman's kit (ruler, brass rail, pencils, pinned paper) carries from the map to the treehouse wall, it has the richest lobby and the largest shop rules text, and its combat depth is good; it holds at both 1600x900 and 1280x800. Its weaknesses are letter-only door tags, partly hidden Companions and the open upper-left plates. AMAZONITE is a close second, with the best party and the most solid toolbar tray, but its shop panels look off-palette and at 1280x800 its tray covers a door. RHYOLITE wins map-vote on its portrait pins and net-plate on its candle plate, but its party is a tight queue and its toolbar tiles are the flattest of the three object toolbars. All 14 map controls appear in every candidate; only LARIMAR presents them as a web toolbar.

candidates.worst_problem: The Kids stand in a tight police-lineup row with heads on one line, smaller than the other builds, and the chinchilla peers out behind the door's edge and the Wisp sits on Bones (1600x900 and worse at 1280x800, where the mouse is nearly lost against the door).

The upper-left plates are a dimmer single-weight frame without the samples' bright double gold rule, and the front red-haired Kid's magnifier presses against the door at 1600x900 while the plates' right edge crowds the back Kid at 1280x800.

The party collapses into one clump where two Kids are reduced to hair and legs and three Companions are hidden, the upper-left plates are flat thin-ruled boxes, and at 1280x800 a Kid's head covers the HOUSE RULE sign.
Bones is half behind a Kid's legs and goes dim, especially at 1280x800, the Wisp is small at both sizes, and the Weak tag straddles the Amina plate's lower-left rim.

In the ruler toolbar the tan control buttons read as flat tags and the Eraser is a flat pink block beside greyed Undo and Clear; at 1280x800 the third portrait also strings far from its door on a leader line. All 14 controls are present and legible at both sizes.

Door choices are only initials on plum plaques that sit over the room labels, the status strip has no faces, and the wooden tray crops the 'NOT a coat rack' note at both sizes. All 14 controls are present and legible.

The notes toolbar is a flat brown bar of plain rectangular web buttons at both sizes, and the door tags are faint stacked initials that you must hunt for. All 14 controls are present, but Undo and Clear are faint.

The ruler-and-brass-rail toolbar is a true drawn object, but its stitched tan buttons are cramped and its zoom discs dark at 1280x800, and the pinned paper tags show initials rather than faces, so door choices need reading. All 14 controls are present.

The hanging plate wraps its message onto a stub line and is deep for its content; at 1280x800 it hides the sconce's lower half and ends close to How to play. Every enemy sign and plate stays visible at both sizes.
The tall upper-right panel reads as a docked dialog and swallows the sconce; at 1280x800 its left edge touches the BUFF sign and its medallion crowds How to play. Signs remain visible at both sizes.
The plain rounded box covers the House Rule medallion at 1600x900 and at 1280x800 cuts the sign to 'SE RULE' and hides the party's heads, so an enemy's sign is lost.

The chained one-line plate is deliberate and clears every sign at both sizes, but at 1280x800 its left chain crosses the trophy strip and its right chain crosses 'Turn 1', and it covers the sconce's base; the slashed-line medallion icon is also obscure.

The seed sits as a bright gold pill floating in the bottom bar like a pasted sticker, and the lower wall holds only a small window and rope; nothing is cut off at either size, though the 1280x800 window sits close to the banner.

The tiny window and rope float unmoored on the lower wall, and the rectangular seat plates are heavier than the samples' cartouche nameplates; the tied seed tag is good but runs toward the right window at 1280x800.
At 1600x900 the window and rope peer out cut-off behind seats 1 and 4, at 1280x800 the lower wall is empty, and at both sizes the unbacked instruction text collides with the hanging stars.

The pinned blueprint, pencil, ruler and rope enrich the lower wall without a collision, but the blueprint's sketch lines are thin and the props sit tight above the panel at 1280x800; the red stamp is also a little faint on the parchment.
The rules panels have a painted ink wash, but its blotchy corners and hard-edged teal and oxblood fields lean toward swatches at both sizes, with modest text floating in a large field.
The rules panels' grey-washed leather is the palest thing on the card at both sizes and reads as a pasted swatch that desaturates the card's blue and oxblood.
The rules panels are so dark that the damask barely registers as a surface at either size, leaving modest text in a near-empty field with only a faint shield watermark.
The tooled-leather rules panels carry the larger, clearest text at both sizes, but the saturated blue and red inset has a hard rectangular edge inside the frame and still hints at a swatch.

winner_fixes: map-vote, door tags beside the chosen rooms: put each friend's painted Kid portrait in a small gold medallion on the pinned paper tag, keeping the initial, so door choices read at a glance without reading letters.
map-vote, bottom status strip: seat the four Kid faces on the torn parchment, with the undecided friend darkened, so the strip shows who has chosen as well as saying it.

map-vote, toolbar buttons: give the tan Hand, Undo, Clear, X room, Unmark, You are here and Overview buttons more height and clearer gaps at 1280x800, keeping the current text size or larger, and lessen the dotted end-stitching that makes them busy.
map-vote, toolbar zoom buttons and selected tool: paint the minus and plus as purple enamel discs with bright gold rims, and give the active Hand a lit gold state so the current tool is obvious.

combat-party, party's left side: bring Bones forward from behind the Kid's legs and remove its dimming, especially at 1280x800, and enlarge the Wisp so all four Companions are recognisable beside their Kids.
combat-party, party scale: raise the front-row Kid scale and let the rows differ more in size so the group has real depth, while keeping the back-left Kid clear of the plate column at 1280x800.
combat-party, upper-left plates: move the Weak tag fully onto the plate surface so it no longer straddles the rim beside the medallion at either size.

net-plate, top right at 1280x800: reroute the hanging chains so they do not cross the trophy strip or 'Turn 1', move the plate clear of the sconce's base, and replace the obscure slashed-line medallion with a candle.
lobby-party, lower wall: strengthen the blueprint's sketch lines and darken the red HOUSE NO. stamp ink, and give the pencil and T-square a little more air above the WHO YOU BRING panel at 1280x800.
shop, rules panels: feather the tooled leather's inner edge under the gold frame and deepen the blue and oxblood slightly, so the inset reads as part of the card rather than a placed rectangle.

grafts.idea: Map door choices shown as gold-ringed Kid portrait medallions on leader lines with a small letter tag beneath, the clearest at-a-glance vote of any candidate.
Four Kid-face medallions in the map's status strip, with the undecided seat darkened.
Purple enamel zoom discs with bright gold rims in the map toolbar, directly echoing the samples' round buttons.
The candle medallion on the net plate, a clearer and more in-world emblem than the slashed line.
Combat party staging: a larger front Kid, stronger size difference between rows, and Companions spread in a readable group to the left, which gave the best recognition of all eight figures.
The toolbar's lit gold selected state and hand icon on the active Hand tool.

verdicts.verdict: No candidate fits between the samples: none reaches coherence 9 on any screen, and all are incremental improvements rather than the same painted hand. VARISCITE is the most coherent system. It treats the party's business as drawn objects throughout: a ruler and brass rail toolbar, pinned paper tags, torn parchment, a rubber stamp, a pencil, a T-square, tooled leather and a chained plate. It wins net-plate, lobby-party and shop outright. Its weakness is map-vote, where initials and a faceless status strip are slower to read than RHYOLITE's portraits, so that graft matters most. AMAZONITE stages the best readable party in combat at both sizes. RHYOLITE has the clearest vote and all 14 map controls legible, but its lobby seed pill and lineup party are weaker. At 1600x900 VARISCITE's map toolbar and lobby props are well spaced; at 1280x800 its toolbar buttons, Bones, the net plate's chains and the lobby props all tighten and need the listed fixes, though nothing is lost. LARIMAR is the clear last on every map, combat, net and lobby measure: a web toolbar, hidden Kids, a plate covering the House Rule sign at both sizes, and props cut off behind seats at 1600x900.
